summary: Neo Verb in Plate mode: Pedal Plate's Decay (a loop gain in percent) becomes a decay time in seconds as measured, scaled by Size; damping, pre-delay, low cut, modulation and mix carry over.

rules.why: measured: Pedal Plate's T30 on a noise burst at Size 100 % (rebuzz-headless), 0.56 s at 0 % to 16 s at 100 %; the tank's delays scale with Size, and so does the time
both default to the middle (Pedal 100 % of 10–200 %, Neo 50 %)

the tank's one-pole low-pass, coefficient Damping × 0.88, has its corner at −ln(d)·44100/2π (its source); Neo Verb's High damping is where the highs start dying faster, so the corner goes twice as high (measured: the same brightness of the tail), from 1 kHz to 20 kHz
both 0–100 %; the depths' scales differ (Pedal Plate swings its tank's taps by up to 16 samples)

unmapped.why: an outer loop from the output back to the input; Neo Verb has none (its Decay sets the tail).

remarks: Both are plates (Pedal Plate is Dattorro's; Neo Verb's Plate mode a dense feedback delay network): the decay time, level and brightness carry over, the echo pattern of the first few tens of milliseconds doesn't.

tolerance.measured: rebuzz-headless (Linux), Neo Poly noise and saw notes through it, each side read against its input: loudness within ±1.5 dB (−0.8 … +1.5); third octaves within ±2.6 dB with the dry sound in (Mix 30 %, 50 %), within ±6 dB wet only (Mix 100 %: the lowest band, and a saw's harmonics, where the two plates' resonances fall differently)

evidence: ExternalMachines/source/thepedal/pedal-plate/PedalPlate.cs: decay = Decay/100 × 0.94, damping = Damping/100 × 0.88 (one-pole), low cut 20–800 Hz exponential, Mix wet against dry

Decay times measured with tools/headless-replace.py's renders: Schroeder T30 of a 20 ms noise burst, Pedal Plate at Damping 0, Size 100 %, modulation off; Neo Verb Plate's Decay measured the same way lands within 2 %
